subject: Budget range validation — token volumes & procurement thresholds (PayBridge)
messages:
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@paybridge.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap & a couple quick asks — PayBridge pricing

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can get a formal quote over to procurement:

1) Recap of product fit
- You want Redwood for normalization and contextual routing across your fraud chat and reconciliation pipelines (low-latency chat + batch embeddings).
- Main constraint: predictable unit economics for volume spikes around end-of-month settlements.

2) Info we need to confirm pricing scenarios:
- Expected monthly token volume (low/typical/high)
- Target budget band ($/month) and target unit economics (target $/1M tokens)
- Procurement approval threshold (monthly spend that triggers PO/contract review)
- Billing terms preference (Net30/PO/CC) and procurement points of contact

3) Next steps
- If you can confirm the three numbers above I’ll put together 2 pricing options (hosted pay-as-you-go + 12-month committed discount) and an example monthly cost table.
- I attached a 1-pager draft pricing sheet and pulled your estimated usage from the summary you shared — see attachment.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a draft quote once I have the volumes and procurement threshold.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: paybridge_usage_report_Q1.csv (summary export)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@paybridge.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Lakhani <maya.lakhani@paybridge.com>, tomas.rivera@paybridge.com
Date: 2026-02-21T10:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & a couple quick asks — PayBridge pricing

Thanks Dylan — good call. A few answers below so you can build scenarios: 

- Monthly token volume (best guess): low 20M / typical 40M / high 60M tokens per month. High is during month-end reconciliation runs and peak fraud investigation windows.
- Budget band: we're aiming to keep this in the $10k–$25k/month window initially.
- Target unit economics: our internal target is roughly $300–$450 per 1M tokens to make the math work for our margins.
- Procurement thresholds: anything above $20k/month will need procurement and legal involvement (contract review + PO). Below $20k we can do SOW + invoice.
- Billing: Prefer PO & Net30 for enterprise purchases. Procurement lead is Maya Lakhani (cc'd); contracting is Tomas Rivera.

Can you show estimated monthly costs for the typical (40M) and high (60M) scenarios at a couple of per-1M price points? Also confirm whether committed capacity pricing tiers and PO billing are supported.

Appreciate it — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product — Platform
PayBridge

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@paybridge.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-22T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & a couple quick asks — PayBridge pricing

Samir — thanks for the clear answers. Attached is a short pricing proposal (redwood_pricing_proposal.pdf) and the quick table below. I included three unit-price scenarios (pay-as-you-go, 12-month commit, and Dedicated reserved capacity estimate). All numbers are illustrative and we’ll formalize in the quote: 

Scenario A — Hosted PAYG
- $/1M tokens: $450
- 40M tokens => $18,000/month
- 60M tokens => $27,000/month
- Billing: monthly invoice (CC/PO possible), no minimum commit

Scenario B — 12-month committed
- $/1M tokens: $325 (committed 12 months, ramp allowed)
- 40M tokens => $13,000/month
- 60M tokens => $19,500/month
- Billing: monthly invoice with committed spend schedule; PO + Net30 supported

Scenario C — Dedicated / Reserved capacity (for predictability)
- Effective $/1M tokens: ~$250 (depends on exact commit & model mix)
- Estimate: 40M => $10,000/month; 60M => $15,000/month
- Requires 3–12 month reservation and sizing call

Notes on cost reduction:
- Caching/prefix-KV and model selection can reduce effective tokens by ~10–30% depending on read/write mix (we can run an eval on your sample workload).
- Quantization + batching recommendations could further lower costs for batch embedding/score workloads.

Procurement & billing: we support PO + Net30 for committed contracts. For PAYG smaller invoices we can accept monthly PO or CC.

If we want to get formal approval from procurement (given the $20k threshold you mentioned), best next step is:
- I’ll produce a formal quote for Scenario B at $325/1M with an initial 3-month ramp schedule that keeps month 1–2 lower and month 3 at typical volume.
- We’ll include standard SOW language and a draft SLA.

Would you like that quote sent to Maya + Tomas directly, or should I send to you first for internal review?

Thanks — attaching the PDF now.
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@paybridge.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Lakhani <maya.lakhani@paybridge.com>, tomas.rivera@paybridge.com
Date: 2026-02-24T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & a couple quick asks — PayBridge pricing

Dylan — this is helpful, thanks. Procurement path confirmed: anything at or above $20k/mo requires a formal quote + SOW + PO. Maya will lead procurement review; Tomas will pick up contracting redlines.

Please send the formal quote for Scenario B (12-month committed at $325/1M) with the ramp schedule you mentioned. Include: 
- Line-item monthly cost table for months 1–6 (we expect to finalize on month 3)
- Statement of work / delivery milestones (integration support + 2-week onboarding)
- Standard data protection language + SOC2 mention
- Billing: PO + Net30 (please confirm acceptance in the quote)

We typically need the formal quote and SOW in hand before procurement will engage — please send to maya.lakhani@paybridge.com and tomas.rivera@paybridge.com and cc me.

If you can get that over by end of week we’ll try to run it through procurement the following week.

Thanks,
Samir
